definition: The overthinking half of OptimalThinkingBench: 1327 general-domain plus 133 math questions, built via constrained synthetic generation and filtered by requiring 8/8 agreement across independently sampled LLM responses so only unambiguous, easy questions survive. It's paired with UnderthinkingBench and scored via AUC_OAA/F1^otb; thinking models on it generate 100-3300+ thinking tokens on trivially simple questions.

evidence.note: Introduces OptimalThinkingBench, a unified benchmark pairing OverthinkingBench (simple queries) and UnderthinkingBench (hard reasoning/math) with a shared F1 metric, showing that none of 33 evaluated LLMs balances accuracy and thinking-token efficiency.
evidence.title: OptimalThinkingBench: Evaluating Over and Underthinking in LLMs
